# Look, Motion, and Sound Requirements Quality Checklist: Modern Style, Smoother Motion, and Sound Fixes

**Purpose**: Validate that the subjective requirements (modern, smooth, stylish, soft, audible) and the sound-reliability requirements are quantified, consistent with the plan, and objectively verifiable before tasks are written
**Created**: 2026-10-22
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope decisions** (defaults applied because no inline arguments were given): depth Standard; audience Reviewer (sign-off before `/speckit-tasks`); focus the two clusters with the most open risk, namely (1) the sound requirements, where the fix cannot be proven for Safari and iPhone from here, and (2) the motion and look requirements, which rest on words such as "smooth", "modern", and "stylish". Requirements carried unchanged from feature 001 (rules, persistence, privacy) are excluded.

## Sound: Audibility and Reliability

- [ ] CHK001 Is "a normal device volume" (the level at which the player must hear each effect) quantified, or does it rest only on the peak range in SC-006? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-014, §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK002 Does SC-006 state where its levels are measured (before or after the game's own playback processing), given it says "as the game plays them"? [Clarity, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK003 Is "loudest and quietest of the five differ by no more than 3 decibels" defined as a peak difference, a perceived-loudness difference, or both? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK004 Is "promptly ... no audible delay behind the motion" given a latency threshold, so it can be judged without a listening opinion? [Measurability, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK005 Is "comfortable" (loudness, no startling) defined by a measurable limit rather than listener opinion? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010, §US2-3]
- [ ] CHK006 Is "every supported desktop and phone browser" tied to a stated list (feature 001's browser matrix), or left as a phrase that depends on another document? [Dependency, Spec §FR-014, §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK007 Does the spec say what must happen on reload when sound was saved as on, given feature 001 requires settings to be restored (its FR-033) and the plan shows the control as off until the first gesture? [Conflict, Spec §FR-014, Plan §Audio contract]
- [ ] CHK008 Are the requirements for returning to sound after an interruption (a phone call, switching tabs, the device locking) stated in the spec, or only in the plan? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK009 Is it specified what the player is told, if anything, when sound is on but the device's hardware silent switch or volume prevents any output? [Gap, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK010 Is "the control shows off instead" in FR-014 matched by a stated requirement for what the saved setting holds in that case? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK011 Do FR-013 ("any sound data is fetched or prepared only when the player first turns sound on") and the edge case about the sound being unavailable offline still describe one coherent behaviour now that no file is fetched? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK012 Is a recovery behaviour defined for a sound that works, then stops partway through a session? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Gap]
- [ ] CHK013 Is "blind trial" in SC-005 defined with the number of listeners, the number of trials, and the pass threshold? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK014 Are the descriptions of each effect (a light tap, a warm two-note chime, a soft reverse-tap, a rising flourish, a soft falling tone) testable, or are they only adjectives a listener must interpret? [Measurability, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK015 Does FR-012 state whether the undo sound also plays when the undo is made from the game-over dialog's own button, as well as the toolbar? [Coverage, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK016 Are requirements stated for sound while the screen-reader announcement for the same event is playing (an undo, a win, game over)? [Gap, Spec §FR-012]

## Motion: Smoothness and Limits

- [ ] CHK017 Is "no visible stepping" quantified (a frame-time limit or a dropped-frame count), or does smoothness rest only on the 60 fps statement and tester opinion? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK018 Is "current mid-range phone" defined with a reference device or class, so SC-003 can be reproduced? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005, §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK019 Does FR-005's 150 ms limit cover the whole move (slide, merge acknowledgement, and the new tile's entrance) as the plan's timeline assumes, or only "slide and merge"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, Plan §Motion contract]
- [ ] CHK020 Is a duration limit stated for the undo and new-game transitions, which FR-004 requires to animate but FR-005 does not cover? [Gap, Spec §FR-004, §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK021 Is a limit stated for how long a keypress may wait before its motion starts, now that input arriving mid-move is queued? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK022 Is "a brief, clearly visible acknowledgement" for a merge quantified (size change, duration), so it is distinguishable from an ordinary slide? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK023 Is "degrades gracefully (shorter or simpler)" defined, including what triggers it on a low-powered phone? [Ambiguity, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK024 Is "removed or reduced to a simple fade" for reduced motion resolved to one behaviour per motion kind, rather than two allowed outcomes? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK025 Does "50 rapid moves ... identical ... in every run" in SC-004 state how many runs, and what "rapid" means in moves per second? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK026 Are hover requirements for controls consistent with touch devices, which have no hover state? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016]

## Look and Palette: Quantification

- [ ] CHK027 Are "calm, soft", "soft depth", and "generous and even spacing" given measurable properties (a radius range, spacing scale, shadow limits), or left to the plan? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK028 Is "tile colours that progress smoothly from low to high values" measurable, for example by a step size between neighbouring tiles? [Measurability, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK029 Is a distinct treatment for values above 1024 defined as a measurable difference from the 1024 tile? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK030 Is "one confident accent colour used sparingly" bounded (which elements may use it, and where it must not appear)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK031 Are the contrast requirements for hover, pressed, and focused states of controls stated, as opposed to the resting state only? [Gap, Spec §FR-016, §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK032 Is the red-green colour-vision simulation in FR-022 and SC-008 specified (which deficiencies, and the pass criterion), given feature 001 left the same gap? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-022, §SC-008]
- [ ] CHK033 Does the spec say how the high-contrast theme should feel under the "calm and soft" direction, or only that it stays high contrast? [Gap, Spec §FR-015, §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK034 Are requirements for the typeface's consistency across devices stated, given the design uses each device's own fonts and so will differ between platforms? [Gap, Spec §FR-015, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK035 Is the update's effect on a player's first look at the redesign (a returning player with a game in progress) described, or only that stored data is preserved? [Coverage, Spec §FR-023, §FR-024]

## Success Criteria and Traceability

- [ ] CHK036 Is "more modern than the current one" in SC-001 anchored to a specific version of the game, so the comparison stays valid after release? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK037 Can SC-001 and SC-002 be satisfied at 5 testers, and are the two success criteria meant to be measured in the same session? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK038 Is there a success criterion for the sound reaching the speaker at an audible level that does not depend on the listener's judgement (the peak range in SC-006 aside)? [Gap, Spec §SC-005, §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK039 Does SC-009 ("zero violations in every theme") name the scanning tool and its rule set, or leave it open as feature 001 did? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-009]
- [ ] CHK040 Is each of the 25 functional requirements covered by at least one success criterion or acceptance scenario, with FR-019, FR-024, and FR-025 checked explicitly? [Traceability, Spec §FR-019, §FR-024, §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK041 Does the spec's reuse of feature 001's rules (the 150 ms limit, the contrast ratios, the size budgets) cite them by requirement ID, so a change to feature 001 cannot silently change this feature? [Traceability, Spec §FR-005, §FR-021, §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK042 Is the traceability gap to the BRD (this refresh cites no BRD requirement ID) recorded as an accepted exception, as the constitution's workflow section requires of specifications? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit.implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit.specify` and `/speckit.clarify`
- Items tagged `[Conflict]` or `[Gap]` are candidates for `/speckit-clarify`. The highest-impact ones are CHK007 (saved sound on versus the control), CHK020 and CHK021 (undo and new-game duration, and input wait), CHK006 (browser list), and CHK009 (silent switch)
- Add comments or findings inline
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
